fields.value: Replication Data for: The Dire Disregard of Measurement Invariance Testing in Psychological Science

dsDescriptionValue.value: In this article, we aimed to assess the degree to which measurement invariance (MI) is tested and indeed holds in psychological studies that aim to compare scale mean scores across (experimental) groups or time. Our goals were to evaluate how often MI is tested, the quality of reporting on MI testing, and how often MI holds in a sample of psychological studies. To this end, we sampled 426 articles with open data from two psychology journals and considered 918 scale mean comparisons (SMC) reported in these articles.

publicationCitation.value: D'Urso, E., Maassen, E., van Assen, M. A. L. M., Nuijten, M. B., De Roover, K., & Wicherts, J. M. (2022, July 26). The Dire Disregard of Measurement Invariance Testing in Psychological Science.

fields.value: The study was preregistered and the preregistration can be found at https://osf.io/s96gc and in the file prere-main-anonymized.pdf. See the file Data Report - Replication Data for - The Dire Disregard of Measurement Invariance Testing in Psychological Science.pdf for, among other things, more information about the files and how they relate.
